plan.intro: Six weeks out. You're riding about 6–7 hours and 105 miles a week, and your longest ride since September is 42 miles, so this block builds endurance first: the long ride grows to 90 miles by Saturday, December 26, then you taper.

plan.race: Race day: hold about 240 W on the pavement and push to about 270 W on the gravel. Ease to about 190 W through the Lake Bastrop singletrack; it's where watts buy the least speed. One stop at the end of the singletrack, 15 minutes at most. Take in 90 g carbs and 500 ml fluid an hour from the start.

goal.title: This year's goals
goal.note: 2027 projection at 250 W NP (about 236 W average): the same group riding as last year and 15 minutes stopped finishes in about 5:48. That's 0.89 of your current FTP for five and a half hours, well above what most riders can hold that long. It's realistic only if your FTP rises toward 300 W by race day, or if you sit in a fast group for most of the day.

top3.note: Last year's 60-mile race was won at 22.6 mph, with a lead group of ten finishing within ten seconds. The 2027 course is 51 miles: at their speed that's about 2:15. At 250 W NP you'd ride about 18.7 mph and finish around 2:43, roughly 28 minutes back. The projection assumes you ride mostly alone. Riding that speed is only possible inside the front group, so the race comes down to holding the first 30 minutes and staying in the draft.
